title: Dennis Lebo v. Susquehanna Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: The Standing Judicial Commission upheld the Panel’s ruling and denied the complaint, answering no to both whether Presbytery erred and whether it affirmed that Session had ceded budget approval to the congregation.
first_summary: A member challenged Presbytery’s approval of a congregational motion supplementing an assistant-pastor fund, arguing that Session had surrendered its exclusive budget authority. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the motion addressed a special circumstance rather than approval of the budget and expressly left the salary figure to the elders and deacons. Session had already approved the budget and retained full control of church funds, so the congregation’s action did not violate BCO 12-5b.
summary: A member challenged Presbytery’s approval of a congregational motion supplementing an assistant-pastor fund, alleging that Session had ceded its budget authority. The SJC denied both issues. The motion addressed a special circumstance, not approval of the budget, and left the salary figure to the elders and deacons; Session had already approved the budget and retained control of church funds. The ruling was confined to the congregation’s particular circumstances and did not approve congregational budget adoption.
